title: Great Organizations Promote Valued Behaviors, Not General Values
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that broad corporate value statements like Respect, Integrity, or Excellence rarely change behavior because they are too abstract for people to apply day to day. Even adding a definition, the author says, only marginally improves how actionable a value becomes. The real shift happens when leaders translate a value into a specific, observable behavior they want team members to practice, such as defining Respect as listening without interrupting. This requires leaders to make explicit choices about what they actually want people to do rather than relying on inspirational but vague language. The piece closes by contrasting the two approaches directly: valued behaviors build culture, while general values mostly serve as marketing copy.
points: Broad value statements (Respect, Integrity, Excellence) are too abstract to influence daily behavior
